title: Brasília march from the Army HQ camp and occupation of the Three Powers buildings
organizer: Not named in opened reporting; a march from the Army HQ encampment was advertised
participants_original: SSP/DF estimated 3,000 near Army HQ before the planned march; on-scene reports describe thousands marching; neither measures entrants to the buildings.
threshold_50_evidence: SSP/DF estimated about 3,000 near Army HQ before the planned march, and the Guardian describes thousands marching. The sources do not provide a count of those who reached or entered the buildings.

start_date.summary: Reports place the march and entry into government buildings on 8 January; S042 also reproduces an SSP/DF estimate near Army HQ that day.

end_date.summary: Opened reports describe police restoring control/clearing the occupied buildings that evening; this day-level endpoint applies to this action only, not the camp or wider campaign.

location.summary: The march proceeded from the Army HQ camp to the Three Powers Plaza in Brasília.

scope.summary: The recorded physical action is at a Brasília government complex; travel from other states does not turn this site into a multi-city protest.

organizer.summary: Reports describe the movement and an advertised march but do not identify a specific organizer.

demands.summary: Reporting describes demands for military intervention and removal/rejection of Lula’s elected government; this is coded as political process and removal demand.

participants_original.summary: SSP/DF estimated about 3,000 near the camp before the march; an on-scene account reports thousands marching. No count of building entrants is given.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: A contemporaneous on-scene report describes thousands marching; the threshold is clear for the march, but not an exact entrance count.

protester_violence.summary: Opened reports describe forced entry and vandalism of government buildings.

state_response.summary: Police/federal forces retook the buildings and arrested more than 300 people. Arrests and crowd dispersal are yes; accommodation, beatings, ignore, killings and shootings remain unknown.

notes: This discrete January 8 march and occupation occurred from a pre-existing post-election Army HQ camp. The distinction between a new event and an action within the older campaign, and its monthly owner, remain unresolved. The January 9 camp clearances do not establish that the wider campaign ended.
open_questions: Resolve whether the Jan 8 march/occupation is a distinct event or belongs to the pre-month anti-election campaign and identify the proper owner unit.
No count is available for marchers who reached or entered government buildings; keep the reported pre-march camp estimate separate.
Review protester violence and the two documented response measures against the coding manual; all other response dimensions remain unknown.

title: São Paulo Paulista Avenue march against the January 8 attacks
location: São Paulo: MASP/Paulista Avenue toward Praça Roosevelt
organizer: Unions and social movements; individual conveners not fully enumerated
participants_original: Folha reports no Military Police estimate; Guilherme Boulos claimed more than 50,000 participants.
threshold_50_evidence: The only reported number is Boulos’s claim of more than 50,000; the police gave no estimate. Attribute the threshold evidence to the participant, not an official count.

start_date.summary: Folha dates the evening march to 9 January.

end_date.summary: Folha describes the march route toward Praça Roosevelt on 9 January; no finer closing time is coded.

location.summary: The march ran from the MASP/Paulista Avenue area toward Praça Roosevelt.

scope.summary: This is a single São Paulo march, not an aggregation with separate events in other cities.

organizer.summary: Folha says unions and social movements called the march; it does not enumerate all organizers.

demands.summary: Marchers demanded punishment for attackers, no amnesty and accountability for funders, and defended democracy.

participants_original.summary: Folha says the police provided no estimate and attributes a claim of more than 50,000 to Guilherme Boulos.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Boulos’s attributed “more than 50,000” claim exceeds the threshold; it is not an official or independent estimate.

protester_violence.summary: The report does not establish violence or its absence at this march; code unknown.

state_response.summary: No response in any of the seven coded dimensions is documented for this march in the opened report; retain unknown for each.

notes: A separate evening march from Paulista Avenue toward Praça Roosevelt. Do not substitute the earlier USP Law School estimate or counts from other cities. Participant violence and state responses are unknown because this report does not document them.
open_questions: Seek an independent attendance estimate if available; the reported threshold rests on Boulos’s public claim.
No source in this first pass resolves the seven state response dimensions or protester violence.

threshold_50_evidence: Folha reports approximately 800 people, comfortably over 50; this is the separate earlier university gathering, not the later Paulista march count.

start_date.summary: Folha reports an earlier USP Law School gathering on 9 January before the evening Paulista march.

end_date.summary: The opened report does not establish when this gathering ended.

location.summary: The earlier assembly took place at the USP Law School in São Paulo.

scope.summary: This is a separate local university gathering as described by Folha.

organizer.summary: Folha describes the gathering as involving USP students but names no organizer.

demands.summary: The gathering rejected the attacks and defended democracy.

participants_original.summary: Folha reports about 800 people at the USP Law School gathering.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The source’s approximate estimate of about 800 exceeds 50.

protester_violence.summary: The report does not establish violence or its absence at this gathering; code unknown.

state_response.summary: No response in any of the seven coded dimensions is documented for this gathering; retain unknown for each.

notes: Folha distinguishes an earlier gathering at USP Law School from the later Paulista Avenue march. Keep them separate pending review of whether the actions were coordinated parts of one event; do not merge or double-count participants.
open_questions: Resolve the boundary between the earlier USP gathering and the later Paulista march; no participant overlap is quantified.
No physical end time or state response is reported.

title: Manaus gathering at the Isaac Sabbá refinery access roads
location: Manaus, Amazonas: access roads to the Isaac Sabbá refinery
organizer: Not named; report identifies Bolsonarista protesters attempting to block refinery access
participants_original: FUP reported approximately 50 people near the access roads at 07:00; none were present about an hour later.
threshold_50_evidence: The only estimate is approximately 50, so the ≥50 threshold remains uncertain; do not round it up or transfer counts from other refinery sites.

start_date.summary: The source reports an approximate gathering near the refinery access around 07:00 on 9 January.

end_date.summary: The source says no one was there about an hour later, supporting a day-level end for the observed gathering.

location.summary: The article locates the group near the access roads to the Isaac Sabbá refinery in Manaus.

scope.summary: This candidate covers only the Manaus site and does not aggregate refinery sites in other states.

organizer.summary: The report does not identify an individual organizer for the Manaus group.

demands.summary: The reported immediate activity was an attempt to block fuel distribution; no explicit domestic-government demand for this group is stated.

participants_original.summary: FUP reported about 50 people at 07:00 and none there roughly one hour later.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: An approximate count of 50 is borderline; the threshold cannot be resolved from this report.

protester_violence.summary: The source does not establish violence or its absence at the Manaus gathering.

state_response.summary: The article reports police activity at other sites, but does not establish any of the seven response dimensions for this Manaus group.

notes: The opened Folha report, with explicit Reuters contribution, describes an attempt to block fuel distribution. It does not state a specific demand directed to Brazil’s government for this Manaus group. Other states’ sites and police responses are not transferred to Manaus.
open_questions: Clarify whether this group made a demand directed to the domestic government or its policy, rather than only attempting to interrupt fuel distribution.
The approximate count of 50 is borderline; no exact count is reported.
Confirm whether this January 9 gathering is a new episode or another action in the pre-month post-election campaign.

title: Porto Alegre World Social Forum opening march

organizer: World Social Forum participants/organizers; individual leads not specified
participants_original: Brasil de Fato describes thousands marching; it provides no exact number.
threshold_50_evidence: The opened report says thousands attended, establishing ≥50 without converting the qualitative figure into an exact count.

start_date.summary: The organizer announcement planned the march for 25 January; contemporaneous follow-up reports that it took place that day.

end_date.summary: No source reviewed establishes when the march ended.

location.summary: The march gathered at Largo Glênio Peres/Paço Municipal and proceeded through Porto Alegre’s historic center.

scope.summary: This candidate is the Porto Alegre opening march, not all World Social Forum sessions or separate city actions.

organizer.summary: The event was announced as the World Social Forum opening march; individual conveners are not specified.

demands.summary: Participants voiced varied demands involving indigenous land, democracy, health, public policy, worker rights and accountability. The source does not show all were shared by all marchers.

participants_original.summary: Brasil de Fato describes thousands at the march; no exact number is given.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: “Thousands” establishes a crowd above 50; no exact count or interval is inferred.

protester_violence.summary: The report does not establish violence or its absence; code unknown.

state_response.summary: The organizer announcement and report do not document the seven state-response dimensions; retain unknown for each.

notes: The opening march was an executed public gathering of thousands. Interviews describe diverse demands; a shared domestic-government target across participants is not established. Keep the delivery-worker subgroup and its private-platform dispute distinct from the whole march.
open_questions: Determine whether the march had a shared demand directed to Brazil’s government/policy or only diverse group-specific demands.
